label: Progress gain
summary: The amount of progress the innovation gains when its monthly progress chance succeeds.
details: Vanilla's innovation tooltip says there is a chance each month to gain this much progress, next to the chance from GetProgressChance. The game does not document its return type.

label: Progress gain breakdown
summary: A text that lists what adds up to the innovation's progress gain.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a shared tooltip (cooltip). Going by its name, it is the breakdown of the value from GetProgressGain; the game documents nothing more.

label: Innovation type
summary: The innovation type (the kind of innovation) of this cultural innovation.
details: Vanilla asks the result for its name in a localization text, and passes it to a Silk Road check in the culture window.

label: Has bonus progress
summary: Whether the cultural innovation has bonus progress.
details: Going by its name and its bool return type. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Has spread marker
summary: Whether the cultural innovation shows a spread marker.
details: Vanilla uses it only to show or hide parts of the culture window. Going by its name, the marker is tied to the innovation spreading to other cultures; the game documents nothing more.

label: Is active
summary: Whether the cultural innovation is active.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the innovation's button in the culture window. It also uses it in checks for what is visible or clickable: an entry is hidden for the culture head when it is not active, and enabled unless it is neither active nor able to be a fascination. Going by its name; the game does not say what active means exactly.

label: Is fascination
summary: Whether the innovation is the culture's fascination.
details: Vanilla uses it in the culture window as the pressed state of a button and to show or hide a widget. A widget that also checks whether the player can set it as fascination is shown only when this is false. Going by the name, a fascination is the innovation the culture has chosen to focus on.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the cultural innovation is valid.
details: Going by its name and the same function on other types (about a thousand uses of IsValid in all). Vanilla has no use on this type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Select as fascination
summary: Makes this innovation the culture's fascination.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the culture window. Going by its name and that use, the click makes this innovation the fascination.

label: Innovation itself
summary: The cultural innovation itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types (it hands the object to another function). Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Innovation type itself
summary: The innovation type object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Custom text
summary: A text from a named custom text entry, run on the innovation type.
details: It takes one argument, the name of the custom text, and returns text. Going by how Custom is written on other types in vanilla, for example Character.Custom( 'Name' ). Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text to run.

label: Culture era type
summary: The culture era (the stage of cultural development) this innovation type belongs to.
details: Vanilla asks the result for its frame, to pick a picture in the culture window.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the innovation type.
details: Vanilla shows it as the text of a shared tooltip.

label: Effects text
summary: A text that describes what the innovation type does for a given culture.
details: It takes two arguments. Vanilla passes a culture first and the player second, in shared tooltips. Going by the name of its companion HasEffects, check that first to see whether there is anything to show.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are described for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A character; vanilla passes the player (probably the one the text is written for).

label: Group name
summary: The name of the group the innovation type belongs to.
details: Vanilla puts it in front of the word 'innovation' in an innovation tooltip, as in '<group> innovation'.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the innovation type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of image widgets in the culture window and in shared tooltips.

label: Key
summary: The key (script name) of the innovation type, as text.
details: Going by its name and the way GetKey is used on other types, for example in debug texts and to build other keys. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Name
summary: The display name of the innovation type, as text.
details: Going by its name and the very many uses of GetName on other types. The lines vanilla has for this function are Silk Road decision texts that look like they call GetName on something else, so this rests on the name.

label: Progress text
summary: A text about the progress of the innovation type, for the thing passed in.
details: It takes one argument. Going by its name only; vanilla never uses it and the game documents nothing more. The return type is not registered.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented.

label: Has effects
summary: Whether there is an effects text to show for the innovation type, for a given culture and character.
details: It takes the same two arguments as GetEffectsDesc, culture first, then the character. Vanilla uses it to show or hide the effects line of a shared tooltip. Going by the name, it tells whether GetEffectsDesc has anything to say.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are described for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A character; vanilla passes the player.

label: Is active for player
summary: Whether the innovation type is active for the player's culture.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the innovation type is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it in the Silk Road window to show an entry only when it is valid. The game does not say what valid means exactly.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the innovation type into a scope, so script functions such as ScriptValue can be used on it.
details: Going by its name and how MakeScope is used on other types in vanilla, for example GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue( ... ). Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Innovation type itself
summary: The innovation type itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Pillar itself
summary: The culture pillar object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Custom text
summary: A text from a named custom text entry, run on the culture pillar.
details: It takes one argument, the name of the custom text, and returns text. Going by how Custom is written on other types in vanilla. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text to run.

label: Audio parameter
summary: An audio parameter, as text, for the culture pillar.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that calls GetAudioParameter on a culture's heritage in the multiplayer lobby. Vanilla has no line for this exact type, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Cultures with pillar
summary: The list of cultures that have this pillar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for a list widget in the ruler designer window.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the culture pillar, written for a given culture.
details: Vanilla passes a culture and shows it in the pillar tooltips of the culture window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the text is written for.

label: Effects text
summary: A text that lists what the pillar does for a given culture.
details: Vanilla passes a culture and puts it at the top of the pillar tooltip. Use HasEffectDescription to check first whether there is text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are described for.

label: Icon
summary: The icon picture of the culture pillar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the texture of image widgets in the culture window and in the window for diverging a culture.

label: Index
summary: The number of the culture pillar in the game's list of pillars.
details: Going by its name and its int32 return type. The lines vanilla has for GetIndex belong to other types, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Pillar name
summary: The name of the culture pillar (for example a language), as text.
details: Vanilla uses it for languages in effect texts such as "You learn the ... language" and "... learns the ... language".

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the culture pillar as plain text, with no tooltip on it.
details: Vanilla uses it for the court language name, in the court grandeur text, and in the heritage title of the culture window ('<name> Heritage').

label: Pillar type name
summary: The name of the kind of pillar this is, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in a text that says none of the pillar type's effects apply until it is established, and as the text of a tooltip.

label: Pillar type name without tooltip
summary: The name of the kind of pillar as plain text, with no tooltip.
details: Going by its name next to GetTypeName. The vanilla lines found for this name belong to other types (scheme types).

label: Has effects text
summary: Whether the pillar has an effects text for a given culture.
details: Vanilla uses it so that the tooltip adds a line break and the description only when there is something to show.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are described for.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the culture pillar has an icon.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses HasIcon on other types to show an icon only when there is one; it has no line for this type.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the culture pillar is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it in the window for replacing a pillar to show an entry only when it is valid. The game does not say what valid means exactly.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the culture pillar into a scope, so script functions such as ScriptValue can be used on it.
details: Going by its name and how MakeScope is used on other types in vanilla. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Pillar itself
summary: The culture pillar itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to court language functions (adopting a language, court grandeur from the language) and to a map icon click that opens the language view.

label: Reformation itself
summary: The culture reformation object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: New pillar
summary: The pillar that the culture reformation (a change of the culture's pillars or traditions) would bring in.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a shared tooltip, so the tooltip shows that pillar.

label: New tradition
summary: The tradition that the culture reformation would bring in.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of widgets in the culture window and in a tooltip, and in a text 'Replacing with <name>'.

label: Progress
summary: How far the reformation has come, as a number out of 100.
details: Vanilla writes it as 'Progress: x/100' in tooltips and uses it as the value of a progress bar in the culture window.

label: Progress breakdown
summary: A text that lists what makes up the reformation's monthly progress.
details: Vanilla puts it below the 'Monthly Progress' line of the tradition and pillar tooltips while one is being established.

label: Replaced tradition
summary: The tradition that the reformation would replace.
details: Going by its name. The one vanilla line found calls it on a different window object (the add tradition window), so this rests on the name.

label: Time left
summary: The time left until the reformation is done, as text.
details: Vanilla writes it in tooltips as 'x left' and as 'To be established in x'.

label: Is adding new tradition
summary: Whether the reformation is adding a new tradition.
details: Vanilla uses it with the question whether the next tradition slot is available, to show or enable parts of the culture window. Reading the lines, the check is about adding a tradition into a free slot; the game documents nothing more.

label: Is reforming same pillar type
summary: Whether the reformation is changing the same kind of pillar as the pillar given.
details: Vanilla passes the culture's martial or ethos pillar, and also requires that the window is not in reformation mode, to decide whether to show something in the culture window.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The pillar to compare the kind with.

label: Reformation itself
summary: The culture reformation itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Culture template itself
summary: The culture template object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types. A culture template is a culture as offered in the ruler designer.

label: Dynasty coat of arms frame
summary: The frame picture of the dynasty coat of arms that goes with this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as a texture in the coat of arms widget, reached through a bookmark character's dynasty template.

label: Dynasty coat of arms mask
summary: The mask picture that shapes the dynasty coat of arms for this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as the mask of the coat of arms widget.

label: Dynasty coat of arms offset
summary: The shift (a 2D vector) applied to the dynasty coat of arms for this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as the offset of the coat of arms widget.

label: Dynasty coat of arms scale
summary: The size factor (a 2D vector) applied to the dynasty coat of arms for this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as the scale of the coat of arms widget.

label: House coat of arms frame
summary: The frame picture of the house coat of arms that goes with this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as a texture in the coat of arms widget.

label: House coat of arms mask
summary: The mask picture that shapes the house coat of arms for this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as the mask of the coat of arms widget.

label: House coat of arms offset
summary: The shift (a 2D vector) applied to the house coat of arms for this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as the offset of the coat of arms widget. That line reads the dynasty template, not the house one, as the game's own line shows.

label: House coat of arms scale
summary: The size factor (a 2D vector) applied to the house coat of arms for this culture template.
details: Going by its name and a vanilla line that uses it as the scale of the coat of arms widget.

label: Name
summary: The name of the culture template, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ruler designer (the culture list entry and its click tooltip) and in a debug menu.

label: Template data
summary: The data object that belongs to the culture template.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a widget in a debug menu. Going by the type name, the result is a CultureTemplateData.

label: Culture template itself
summary: The culture template itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Vanilla uses it in the ruler designer window, to compare it with the chosen culture's template and to set the culture of the designed ruler.

label: Template data itself
summary: The culture template data object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Dynasty coat of arms frame
summary: The frame picture of the dynasty coat of arms of the culture.
details: Going by its name and vanilla lines that read it as a texture in the coat of arms widgets, after Dynasty.GetCulture. Those lines do not name this type themselves.

label: Dynasty coat of arms frame name
summary: The name of the dynasty coat of arms frame, as text.
details: Going by its name and its CString return type. Vanilla never uses it. The house version is used in a debug menu.

label: Dynasty coat of arms mask
summary: The mask picture that shapes the dynasty coat of arms of the culture.
details: Going by its name and vanilla lines that use it as the mask of the coat of arms widget after Dynasty.GetCulture.

label: Dynasty coat of arms offset
summary: The shift (a 2D vector) applied to the dynasty coat of arms of the culture.
details: Going by its name and vanilla lines that use it as the offset of the coat of arms widget after Dynasty.GetCulture.

label: Dynasty coat of arms scale
summary: The size factor (a 2D vector) applied to the dynasty coat of arms of the culture.
details: Going by its name and vanilla lines that use it as the scale of the coat of arms widget after Dynasty.GetCulture.

label: House coat of arms frame
summary: The frame picture of the house coat of arms of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the coat of arms widgets.

label: House coat of arms frame name
summary: The name of the house coat of arms frame, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it in brackets as text in a debug menu.

label: House coat of arms mask
summary: The mask picture that shapes the house coat of arms of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the mask of the coat of arms widgets.

label: House coat of arms offset
summary: The shift (a 2D vector) applied to the house coat of arms of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the offset of the coat of arms widgets.

label: House coat of arms scale
summary: The size factor (a 2D vector) applied to the house coat of arms of the culture.
details: Vanilla uses it as the scale of the coat of arms widgets.

label: Template data itself
summary: The culture template data itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Tradition itself
summary: The culture tradition object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Custom text
summary: A text from a named custom text entry, run on the culture tradition.
details: It takes one argument, the name of the custom text, and returns text. Going by how Custom is written on other types in vanilla. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text to run.

label: Description
summary: The description text of the tradition, written for a given culture.
details: Vanilla passes a culture and shows it in the tradition tooltip below the effects text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the text is written for.

label: Effects text
summary: A text that lists what the tradition does for a given culture.
details: Vanilla passes a culture and puts it at the top of the tradition tooltip.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The culture the effects are described for.

label: Layered icon
summary: The tradition's icon made of several layers.
details: Vanilla asks it for layer 0 or layer 1 (GetTexture with a layer number) to draw each layer as a texture in the culture window.

label: Tradition name
summary: The name of the cultural tradition, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in effect texts about a culture gaining or losing a tradition ("Gains the ... tradition", "Lost the ... tradition").

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of the tradition as plain text, with no tooltip on it.
details: Vanilla uses it as the text of labels in the culture window and in the window for adding a tradition.

label: Is valid
summary: Whether the tradition is valid.
details: Vanilla uses it in the window for adding a tradition to show an entry only when it is valid. The game does not say what valid means exactly.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the tradition into a scope, so script functions such as ScriptValue can be used on it.
details: Going by its name and how MakeScope is used on other types in vanilla. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Tradition itself
summary: The culture tradition itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the add tradition window, to ask what blocks picking it, to select it, and to check whether it can be picked.

label: Culture window itself
summary: The culture window object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Can predict next spread
summary: Whether the culture window can show a prediction of the next spread (an innovation spreading to the culture).
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide a part of the culture window.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the culture window.
details: Vanilla runs it when a close button is clicked.

label: Confirm reformation cancel
summary: Asks to confirm cancelling the culture reformation.
details: Going by its name and its void return type. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Culture
summary: The culture the window is showing.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of the window's parts, and asks it whether it has a spread.

label: Culture eras
summary: The list of culture eras (stages of cultural development) the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for a list widget in the culture window.

label: Culture head info
summary: A text about the head of the culture.
details: Vanilla passes a character (Character.Self in a text that is shown when the viewer is not the culture head, so probably the head). It shows the result in the culture window and in that text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A character; vanilla passes Character.Self (probably the culture head).

label: Culture traditions
summary: The list of traditions of the culture the window shows.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for list widgets in the culture window.

label: My culture info
summary: A text comparing the viewed culture with the culture of the character given.
details: Vanilla passes the player and adds it after the culture head text when the viewed culture is not the player's. The exact content is not documented.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character whose culture is told about, the player in vanilla.

label: Next spread culture
summary: The culture named in the window's prediction of the next spread.
details: Vanilla writes it in 'Next spread will likely be <innovation> of <culture>'. The game does not say how the culture relates to the spread.

label: Next spread innovation
summary: The innovation that the window predicts will spread next.
details: Vanilla writes its name in 'Next spread will likely be <innovation> of <culture>'.

label: Selected culture era
summary: The culture era (stage of cultural development) that is selected in the window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context, and compares its era with an innovation's era to show or hide parts of the window.

label: Skill level
summary: A skill level, going by its name.
details: Going by its name only. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Hide reformation mode
summary: Leaves reformation mode in the culture window.
details: Vanilla runs it when the window starts and when buttons are clicked. Going by its name, it is the opposite of ShowReformationMode.

label: Is in reformation mode
summary: Whether the culture window is in reformation mode (the mode for changing the culture's pillars and traditions).
details: Vanilla uses it to show or hide parts of the window, also negated in combination with the reformation checks.

label: Culture window itself
summary: The culture window itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Should show my culture info
summary: Whether the window should show the extra text about the viewer's own culture.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to switch between two parts of the culture window.

label: Show reformation mode
summary: Puts the culture window into reformation mode.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the culture window.

label: Curve editor itself
summary: The curve editor object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Configure
summary: Sets up the curve editor.
details: Going by its name and its void return type. Vanilla never uses it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Delete
summary: Deletes something in the curve editor.
details: Going by its name and its void return type. Vanilla never uses it on this type, and the game documents nothing more. The Delete lines vanilla has belong to other types.

label: Curve editor itself
summary: The curve editor itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Curve point itself
summary: The curve point object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Position
summary: The position of the point on the curve, as a 2D vector.
details: Going by its name and its return type. Vanilla has no line for this type; the lines it has for the name belong to council positions.

label: Curve point itself
summary: The curve point itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Message window itself
summary: The custom message window object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Add days
summary: Moves the message's arrival date by the given number of days.
details: Vanilla runs it with 1 or -1 from the plus and minus buttons in the message settings window. A negative number goes back.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many days to add.
fields.values: a whole number, negative to subtract

label: Add months
summary: Moves the message's arrival date by the given number of months.
details: Vanilla runs it with 1 or -1 from the plus and minus buttons in the message settings window. A negative number goes back.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many months to add.
fields.values: a whole number, negative to subtract

label: Add years
summary: Moves the message's arrival date by the given number of years.
details: Vanilla runs it with 1 or -1 from the plus and minus buttons in the message settings window. A negative number goes back.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: How many years to add.
fields.values: a whole number, negative to subtract

label: Close window
summary: Closes the custom message window.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the message settings window.

label: Arrival date
summary: The date the custom message arrives, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label in the message settings window.

label: Description
summary: The text of the custom message, as typed in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it in the message settings window. The edit handler OnEditDescription goes with it.

label: Title
summary: The title of the custom message, as typed in the window.
details: Vanilla shows it in the message settings window. The edit handler OnEditTitle goes with it.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the custom message window is open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the visibility of the window's main widget.

label: Message arrives today
summary: Whether the message is set to arrive today.
details: Vanilla uses its negation as the enabled state of buttons, apparently the ones that move the date backwards; going by that, the date cannot go before today. The game documents nothing more.

label: On edit description
summary: Called when the message text is edited, so the window can take the new text.
details: Vanilla runs it from the text-edited event of the description box.

label: On edit title
summary: Called when the message title is edited, so the window can take the new title.
details: Vanilla runs it from the text-edited event of the title box.

label: Reset
summary: Resets the message window to its starting state.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked. Going by its name, it clears what was typed and the date; the game documents nothing more.

label: Message window itself
summary: The custom message window itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Send message
summary: Sends the custom message from one character to another.
details: Vanilla passes the player twice, from a button click in the message settings window. Which argument is the sender and which the receiver is not documented; going by the order, the sender comes first.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: A character, the player in vanilla (probably the sender).

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A character, the player in vanilla (probably the receiver).

label: Toggle window
summary: Opens the custom message window if it is closed, and closes it if it is open.
details: Vanilla runs it from button clicks in the message settings window. Going by its name and the name of IsVisible.

label: Empty data itself
summary: The empty custom data object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Empty data itself
summary: The empty custom data object itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Filter itself
summary: The list filter object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Name
summary: The name of a list filter, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of filter entries in the shared list widgets.

label: Is enabled
summary: Whether the list filter is switched on.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of a filter checkbox in the shared list widgets.

label: Filter itself
summary: The list filter itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Grouped filter itself
summary: The grouped list filter object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Active filter
summary: The number of the filter that is active in the group.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of a list widget in the shared list widgets.

label: Filters
summary: The list of filters in the group.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for a list widget in the shared list widgets.

label: Group name
summary: The name of the filter group, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as a label in the shared list widgets.

label: Grouped filter itself
summary: The grouped list filter itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: Sorter itself
summary: The list sorter object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Name
summary: The name of a list sorter, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the label of sort entries in the shared list widgets.

label: Sorter itself
summary: The list sorter itself, for passing to other functions.
details: Going by its name and how Self is used on other types. Vanilla has no use of it on this type.

label: List view itself
summary: The list view object itself, used by the game to hand it on to another widget or function.
details: Going by its name only. The lines vanilla has with this name belong to other types.

label: Are filters shown
summary: Whether the filter panel of the list is open.
details: Vanilla uses it as the pressed state of the filter button and as the visibility of the filter panel in the shared list widgets.

label: Active sort number
summary: The number of the sorter the list is sorted by.
details: Vanilla uses it as the selected entry of the sort list widget.

label: Filters
summary: The list of filters of the list view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for list widgets in the shared list widgets.

label: Grouped filters
summary: The list of filter groups of the list view.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for list widgets in the shared list widgets.

label: Sort order
summary: Whether the list is sorted in the first of its two directions (true or false).
details: Vanilla turns it into a frame number (1 or 2) for the sort arrow picture. Which direction is true is not documented.

label: Sorters
summary: The list of sorters the list view offers.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list for the sort list widget.

label: Remove all filters
summary: Switches off every filter of the list.
details: Vanilla runs it when a button is clicked in the shared list widgets.

label: Select group filter
summary: Selects the filter with the given number inside a filter group.
details: Vanilla passes the index of the clicked entry in the list when the selection changes.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The number of the filter to select.
fields.values: a whole number, the index in the list
